frameworks.name: Three Archetypes of Effort
frameworks.definition: A categorization of people by their relationship to effort and completion: the lazy (cannot start), the losers (cannot finish), and the legends (cannot stop).

frameworks.name: Continuous Cycle of Constraint Resolution
frameworks.definition: A repeatable loop: find what works, do more of it, identify what prevents more, solve that constraint, return to doing more.

frameworks.name: Mountain Metaphor for Goal Pursuit
frameworks.definition: Goals are waypoints, not destinations; reaching a summit reveals another mountain beyond. The value is in the climb, not the peak.

claims.text: Goals are mile markers, not finish lines. Upon reaching any revenue target ($10k, $100k, $1M, $10M monthly), the mist lifts and a new goal becomes visible; Hormozi confirms this pattern from personal experience at each milestone.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: The framing resets once external validation (reaching the peak) arrives; goals function as perpetual mile markers rather than terminal states.

claims.text: Critics and naysayers operate from a poverty lens, assuming the climber pursued the mountain for the destination (external validation). They project their own inability to find fulfillment in the process onto those who do. Ignoring their criticism is both rational and necessary.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The person is pursuing ambitious multi-stage goals
Critics are operating from scarcity mindset or poverty mentality
claims.mechanism: Naysayers believe the climber's past goal-achievement (reaching one peak) should have produced permanent happiness; their confusion stems from projecting a happiness-through-destination model onto someone with a climb-for-the-climb motivation structure. This fundamental mismatch makes their criticism unfalsifiable to them.
bounded_by: Does not apply to feedback from people in similar wealth/ambition tier
Does not apply when the critic has relevant domain expertise in scaling

claims.text: Attempting to apply logic to illogical people is itself illogical. When someone makes a decision or statement that does not make sense, the effort to rationalize it is wasted; the person will 'disappear anyway' (exit the sphere of influence).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The person's behavior/statement is fundamentally illogical or misaligned with reality
The relationship is not load-bearing (family, investor, key teammate)
claims.mechanism: Wasting mental effort to rationalize irrationality is an uneconomical allocation of attention; the transient nature of the relationship makes the effort futile.
bounded_by: Does not apply to family relationships where understanding is unavoidable
Does not apply to key employees or business partners where alignment is required

claims.text: The lazy do not know how to start, the losers do not know how to finish, and the legends do not know how to stop. Hormozi explicitly states he would rather be in the legends category and operates tactically on that principle.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: The three archetypes describe a progression of competence: initiation ability, completion ability, and stopping/boundaries inability. The legend tier combines both start and finish capability with the blind spot of knowing when to stop.

anchors.value: can initiate and complete, cannot stop

claims.text: Success in any domain worth playing (health, marriage, business) is not won by winning individual battles; rather, you win by staying alive long enough to outlast everyone else. This frames endurance and continuity as the true competitive edge.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The domain is competitive and multi-year in horizon
claims.mechanism: The business/relationship/health game is not a single-round contest but a multi-round attrition game; the player who compounds effort across years outlasts those who optimize for short-term wins or quit under pressure.
bounded_by: Does not apply to one-time transactional competitions (sports playoffs, exam)
Does not apply to games with fixed endpoints

claims.text: The process of personal growth and business success involves a repeatable cycle: (1) find what works, (2) do more of what works, (3) identify the constraint preventing more, (4) solve that constraint, (5) return to step 2. This loop is the core mechanism of scaling.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: A business or personal domain has achieved initial traction (some repeatable success exists)
The goal is to scale that success
claims.mechanism: Scaling is achieved not through innovation or major pivots, but through obsessive iteration on the constraint of the day. Each cycle removes one constraint, revealing the next limiting factor.
bounded_by: Does not apply to early-stage businesses still searching for what works
Does not apply when 'what works' is fundamentally broken (market rejection)

claims.text: The actual value and motivation in ambitious goal pursuit is the climb (the process and effort), not reaching the mountaintop (the destination or external validation). People who pursue for the climb experience fulfillment at every milestone; those pursuing for the destination experience hollow completion.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The goal requires sustained multi-year effort
The goal involves measurable milestones and rising difficulty
claims.mechanism: Process-oriented motivation (intrinsic) sustains effort across setbacks; destination-oriented motivation (extrinsic) collapses upon arrival because the destination delivers no durable satisfaction. The difference is whether effort itself is the reward.
bounded_by: Does not apply to transactional goals with clear finite endpoints
Does not apply to people primarily motivated by financial security rather than achievement

examples.text: Hormozi recounts a conversation with his father about trying to make sense of another person's irrational decision. His father replied: 'You're trying to apply logic to someone who's illogical, and that itself is illogical.' This insight demonstrates that the effort to rationalize irrational behavior wastes mental energy and should be abandoned in favor of ignoring the person entirely.

Hormozi has personally hit multiple revenue milestones ($10k, $100k, $1M, $10M monthly) and confirms that upon reaching each peak, the mist lifts and another mountaintop becomes visible. He did not experience permanent satisfaction at any milestone, validating the mountain metaphor that goals are continuous waypoints, not terminal destinations.

practices.text: When someone makes a decision or statement that does not make sense to you, ignore it and expect the person to disappear from your life anyway. Do not invest mental effort in rationalizing illogical behavior.

Identify what works in your business or personal life, then obsessively find ways to do more of it. When you hit a ceiling, diagnose the specific constraint blocking more, solve it, and return to doing more.

Choose to be a legend (someone who can start and finish but cannot stop) rather than lazy or a loser. Operate with the assumption that you will pursue ambitious multi-stage goals across your lifetime and structure your life accordingly.
Frame your goals as mile markers, not finish lines. After hitting a goal, immediately set the next one; the mist lifts upon arrival and another peak becomes visible.
